summary: This article explains how rivers form, why they have carried people, goods, and ideas for thousands of years, and examples of great rivers on every continent.
introduce: Show the title “Rivers: Nature's Highways” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: a path that water flows through
good for growing many healthy plants
to cover land with water that has risen or spread

challengeTerms.def: small pieces of soil, sand, or rock carried and left behind by water
the supplying of water to land or crops using channels or pipes
to slowly wear away land or rock, usually by water or wind

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that rivers matter less today than they did long ago, now that people have roads and airplanes? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain why rivers were especially important for trade and farming before modern roads and vehicles existed.
struggling: Pre-teach channel, fertile, and flood with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses sediment, irrigation, and erode to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
